description: Qingsong Xu and colleagues publish FloodCastBench, a dynamic flood-modelling benchmark covering Pakistan 2022, Mozambique 2019, Australia 2022 and the United Kingdom 2015. Zenodo lists one public ZIP under CC BY 4.0 at no cost. The described folders contain 480 m low-fidelity and 30 m or 60 m high-fidelity flood sequences, with TIFF frames every 300 seconds, plus elevation, land cover, rainfall, initial conditions and georeferencing. The authors say hydrodynamic simulations were calibrated with flood observations. These data can train or test flood-forecast surrogates and compare cross-region transfer before using predictions in infrastructure exposure analysis. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this four-event benchmark. A limitation is that the archive is about 21.6 GB and was not downloaded, so actual folder contents, frame counts and calibration quality remain unverified. Simulated inundation is not a direct observation or an approved flood-depth map.
